accepted.question_text: Determine whether every three-dimensional topological manifold that is closed and simply-connected must be homeomorphic to the 3-sphere.

evidence.quote: Any three-dimensional topological manifold which is closed and simply-connected must be homeomorphic to the 3-sphere.
For his proof of the Poincaré conjecture, Perelman was awarded the Millennium Prize on March 18, 2010.

accepted.question_text: Let E be an elliptic curve over the rational numbers with rank r. Determine whether the Hasse-Weil L-function L(E, s) associated with E vanishes to order r at s = 1.

evidence.page: Unsolved problems > Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
evidence.quote: More specifically, the Millennium Prize version of the conjecture is that, if the elliptic curve E has rank r, then the L-function L(E, s) associated with it vanishes to order r at s = 1.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a non-singular complex projective variety. Determine whether every Hodge class on X, meaning a class in H^{2k}(X, Q) ∩ H^{k,k}(X), is a linear combination with rational coefficients of the cohomology classes of complex subvarieties of X.

evidence.quote: Let X be a non-singular complex projective variety. Then every Hodge class on X is a linear combination with rational coefficients of the cohomology classes of complex subvarieties of X.

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with given initial conditions, prove either that smooth, globally defined solutions satisfying the required conditions always exist, or that such smooth solutions do not always exist and the equations can break down.

evidence.page: Unsolved problems > Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness
evidence.quote: The problem, restricted to the case of an incompressible flow, is to prove either that smooth, globally defined solutions exist that meet certain conditions, or that they do not always exist and the equations break down.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every problem for which a proposed solution can be verified quickly, meaning in polynomial time, also has an algorithm that can find a solution quickly; equivalently, determine whether every problem in NP is also in P.

evidence.quote: The question is whether or not, for all problems for which an algorithm can verify a given solution quickly (that is, in polynomial time), an algorithm can also find that solution quickly. Since the former describes the class of problems termed NP, while the latter describes P, the question is equivalent to asking whether all problems in NP are also in P.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2.

evidence.quote: The real part of every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function is 1/2.

accepted.question_text: For any compact simple gauge group G, prove that a non-trivial quantum Yang-Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a positive mass gap Δ > 0, where the mass gap is the difference in energy between the vacuum and the next lowest energy state. The required existence result must establish axiomatic properties at least as strong as those cited in Streater and Wightman (1964) and Osterwalder and Schrader (1973, 1975).

evidence.page: Unsolved problems > Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
evidence.quote: Prove that for any compact simple gauge group G, a non-trivial quantum Yang-Mills theory exists on R^4 and has a mass gap Δ > 0. Existence includes establishing axiomatic properties at least as strong as those cited in Streater & Wightman (1964), Osterwalder & Schrader (1973), and Osterwalder & Schrader (1975).
